objective: Load historical NBA games, with each game's player box score, from the Kaggle 'NBA games' CSV dataset into the Team and Game tables, through a re-runnable backend script, so that the site has real game data without any live feed. First pass: proven against the local dev database; loading the live database is a separate task.
acceptance_criteria: A Team and a Game can be stored with the dataset's own ids and without an API-SPORTS id; each dataset id is unique; every existing row and the API-SPORTS ingestion path keep working.

Running the loader against a directory holding the dataset's teams, games and game-details CSVs stores every NBA team, then every regular-season and playoff game in the chosen seasons, with home and away teams, date, season, both final scores and the box score in the player_stats shape 0x02-events.md documents (player_name, team_id as the internal Team.id, points, rebounds, assists, position).
Preseason and All-Star games are not loaded, and the loader reports how many it skipped.
A game with no final score is skipped and reported, never stored with an invented score.
Season is stored as 'YYYY-YY' (the dataset's start year 2019 becomes '2019-20').
A game or box-score row naming a team the loader does not know stops the load with a message naming it, and leaves the database as it was before that run (fail fast, as 0x02-events.md requires).
Running the loader twice over the same data leaves the same rows: no duplicates, and the second run reports nothing new.
The loader can be limited to named seasons, and says per season how many games it loaded and skipped.
Tests run against a small synthetic CSV fixture with the dataset's column names; the dataset itself is never committed.
A game without an API-SPORTS id never asks the live-score proxy for a score.
